FYI, this is blocking ASP.NET Core trying to use keyed DI. e.g. in frameworks like SignalR, Minimal, MVC, Blazor.

The sooner this gets in the more time we will have to attempt to update the frameworks with support for the feature for 8.0 😃
It's tempting to ask for a preview7 backport even though it is late.

Ok I'm merging it by CET EOD today, given it is blocking ASP.NET Core -- and dotnet/extensions (https://github.com/dotnet/extensions/issues/4211, https://github.com/dotnet/extensions/pull/4222), and NCL...

issue_context.title: Injected or scoped ServiceProvider does not support Keyed services
issue_context.body:
_Originally posted by @CarnaViire in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/89446#issuecomment-1650113376_

Scoped ServiceProvider, acquired from a DI scope created by `IServiceScopeFactory`, _[UPD: or any injected IServiceProvider instance]_ does not implement the `IKeyedServiceProvider`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3dd73e6d53aa7984e9e039b6eb9e7cbc5fec7431/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection/src/ServiceLookup/ServiceProviderEngineScope.cs#L15


Because of that, it is impossible to use Keyed services within HttpClientFactory now, see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/89446

cc @benjaminpetit @halter73 @steveharter

LMK if you need a runnable repro, but it should be along the lines of 
1) Register a keyed singleton
2) Build ServiceProvider, resolve IServiceScopeFactory and create a scope
3) Try to resolve the keyed singleton from scope's service provider.

You'll get an exception System.InvalidOperationException: This service provider doesn't support keyed services.

review_comments: Can we add a reflection based test that verifies that `ServiceProviderEngineScope` implements all the same interfaces that `ServiceProvider` does (except `IDisposable` apparently)? This might catch similar bugs in the future.
